# 周易劄記

## Authors / Editors
- 楊名時 (清朝) 撰 1660 - 1736

**Editions:** WYG

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A Yōngzhèng-Qiánlóng-period *Yìjīng* notebook in two juàn by [楊名時](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%A5%8A%E5%90%8D%E6%99%82) Yáng Míngshí (1660–1736), the principal pupil of [李光地](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E5%85%89%E5%9C%B0) Lǐ Guāngdì and leading transmitter of the Lǐ Guāngdì school of *Yìxué*. The work is undated but post-dates the imperial *Yù zuàn Zhōuyì zhé zhōng* ([KR1a0117](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0117)) of 1715, which it cites in evidence. The work proceeds in *zhájì* 劄記 (notebook) form rather than continuous canonical commentary. While Yáng's exposition of the *Shuōguà zhuàn* and his appended discussion of [朱熹](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E7%86%B9) Zhū Xī's *Qǐ méng* extend the *xiāntiān* diagrammatic tradition (in keeping with his master Lǐ Guāngdì's interest), his canonical exegesis is purely *yìli*-oriented and does not engage in chart-and-numerology speculation. The work is methodologically consistent with the Lǐ Guāngdì line: respectful of Chéng-Zhū without slavish conformity, substantive but not polemical.

The *Sìkù* editors single out the comparison with Yáng's pupil [夏宗瀾](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A4%8F%E5%AE%97%E7%80%BE) Xià Zōnglán (whose *Yì shuō* 易說 records the master-pupil dialogues from Yáng's Yúnnán Governor period): Yáng's master-line exposition surpasses Xià's pupil-elaborations in depth (the editors give the example of *Jiàn yù kòu* 漸禦寇 explained by reference to "wild geese keeping watch by night" as a "shallow" pupil-reading, with Yáng's master-discussion still bearing Lǐ Guāngdì's residue).

**Abstract**

Composition is bracketed by the *Zhōuyì zhé zhōng*'s 1715 publication (which the work cites) and Yáng's death in 1736; the bracket here adopts these dates.

The work is the principal early-eighteenth-century continuation of the Lǐ Guāngdì school of *Yìxué*. Methodologically conservative and Chéng-Zhū-aligned, it represents the orthodox Qiánlóng-court *Yìxué* position — a moderate inheritance of the Kāngxī-period synthesis without the methodological innovations of the contemporary Yán-Lǐ school ([KR1a0140](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0140) [李塨](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E5%A1%A8) Lǐ Gōng) or of the early Qīng *kǎozhèng* tradition (the Huáng brothers, [胡渭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%83%A1%E6%B8%AD) Hú Wèi, [毛奇齡](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%AF%9B%E5%A5%87%E9%BD%A1) Máo Qílíng).

The pairing with Xià Zōnglán's pupil-record *Yì shuō* (separately preserved) gives the work a master-pupil dialogical context. The *Sìkù* editors' explicit comparison — favoring Yáng's master-discussion over Xià's pupil-derivations — is one of the cleaner illustrations in the *Yì*-class tíyào of the editors' attention to intra-school transmission quality.
